Liam Chen: Share benchmark spreadsheet + embedding config recommendations (due: 2026-12-02)

summary: Hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranking for search relevance. Covered embedding models, similarity configs, batching, rerank endpoint flow (candidate generation -> embeddings -> rerank), demoed Console for metrics and Optimize recommendations. Customer concerns: latency for tail queries, cost at scale, data residency and SOC2, and integration with existing Elastic index. Agreed next steps: share pricing, benchmark spreadsheet, and run a pilot using Omnify sample dataset.
topics: Hosted API latency vs cost tradeoffs
transcript:
[15:30] Maya Patel: hi everyone thanks for joining um this is Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. Quick round intro?
[15:31] Carlos Ruiz: hey Carlos here, head of search at Omnify, i'll kick things off on requirements.
[15:31] Priya Singh: Priya, data engineering, i'll handle the data side.
[15:32] Tom Keller: Tom, CTO. looking to improve relevance for web search and in-app discovery.
[15:32] Liam Chen: Liam from Redwood infra/SE, i'll walk the demo and benchmarks.
[15:33] Maya Patel: awesome, goal for today is a hosted API walkthrough for embeddings + rerank, show the console, and talk about pilot steps.
[15:34] Carlos Ruiz: high level we currently use Elastic for retrieval and a lightweight BERT ranker for top10, cost is creeping up, latency for some queries spikes. interested in an embeddings-first flow with rerank.
[15:34] Priya Singh: our dataset is multi-lingual, some docs are large, retention/PII concerns as well.
[15:35] Liam Chen: great, so typical pattern is candidate generation via vector search then a reranker call to the hosted api, we support embeddings endpoints and a rerank endpoint that accepts candidate docs + query, returns a scored ranked list.
[15:36] Tom Keller: what's the end-to-end latency we'd see for top50 -> rerank? our SLA targets are sub-200ms P50 for web queries.
[15:36] Liam Chen: for hosted we see ~80-150ms P50 for small rerank models on GPU for a top10 rerank, top50 will add some time, typically 150-300ms depending on model size and sequence lengths; we can push lower with batching and smaller models.
[15:37] Carlos Ruiz: hmm 300ms tail could be a problem for interactive search, do you support regional routing? we'd like EU data residency.
[15:37] Maya Patel: yes regional routing and model pinning are supported; also Dedicated/Private if you need on-prem or VPC. For this pilot we'll do hosted EU region and show caching/batching suggestions from Optimize.
[15:38] Priya Singh: security questions: SOC 2, KMS for keys, retention and audit logs?
[15:38] Liam Chen: Redwood has SOC2, customer-configurable retention, audit logs in Console, and KMS integration for key management. i'll follow up with the security pack.
[15:39] Maya Patel: i'll include SOC2 report and a KMS integration note in the follow up.
[15:40] Liam Chen: starting the demo, opening the Console, here's the model catalog — note we have several embedding variants (512/768 dims etc). for search you typically want 768/1024 for semantic richness but that increases storage and compute.
[15:41] Carlos Ruiz: what about quantized models, do you do 8-bit / 4-bit for embeddings?
[15:41] Liam Chen: embeddings are usually float16/float32 but we do quantized variants for generator models; for vector search you can compress embeddings or use product quantization on your index side (e.g., pinecone or faiss).
[15:42] Priya Singh: we want to keep our existing ES index for candidate generation; can we integrate?
[15:42] Liam Chen: absolutely. typical pattern: ES for boolean/faceted filters + ANN store (Faiss/Pinecone) for vectors; Redwood embeddings API returns vector blobs you can upsert into your existing index. rerank pipeline can call ES candidates then call our /v1/rerank endpoint.
[15:43] Maya Patel: demoing rerank endpoint now, payload structure: query, candidates (id, text, metadata), config flags for length penalties, and an optional explain token.
[15:44] [15:44] Liam Chen: (typing) sending sample request... response comes back with scores, normalized ranks, and we can stream partial scores for long docs. note transcription: sometimes the console labels are "Redwoood" which is an auto transcription bug.
[15:45] Tom Keller: can we run a batched rerank for many queries to amortize overhead?
[15:45] Liam Chen: yes, our API supports batching of multiple query/candidate sets in one call, also supports async jobs for large bulk reranks and you can configure concurrency in Console Optimize.
[15:46] Priya Singh: cost model—how is pricing calculated for embeddings and rerank?
[15:46] Maya Patel: hosted pricing: embeddings per vector call (per 1k vectors) + rerank per token or per candidate depending on model. i'll attach pricing tiers; for pilots we can offer a pilot discount.
[15:47] Carlos Ruiz: curious about failure modes—what happens if the hosted region is overloaded? do you have fallbacks?
[15:47] Liam Chen: yes, smart routing can fallback to a compatible model variant or another region; we also provide circuit-breaker settings in Console so your app can degrade gracefully.
[15:48] [15:48] Carlos Ruiz: ok show me an end-to-end example with our sample query...
[15:48] Liam Chen: demoing a sample: query -> ES filter -> embed query -> nearest neighbors -> rerank top50 -> final top10. here's the time breakdown in Console: embedding 45ms, retrieval 20ms, rerank 140ms. total ~205ms in this sample.
[15:49] Tom Keller: that's promising, tail behavior?
[15:50] Liam Chen: tail depends on sequence lengths and batch size, Optimize recommends shorter truncation and dynamic batching for your traffic to reduce tail latency. we also have prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts.
[15:50] Priya Singh: about model drift — can we run evals and track quality regressions?
[15:50] Liam Chen: yes, Redwood Optimize lets you tie prompt sets/evals to deployments and alerts on regressions; you can also A/B rollouts in Console.
[15:51] Carlos Ruiz: do you have an integration for our SSO? we need SAML and RBAC for different teams.
[15:51] Maya Patel: yes SSO with SAML/SCIM, RBAC roles, and audit logs are available for enterprise and configurable in Private deployments.
[15:52] Tom Keller: for the pilot we'll need an NDA and a short contract.
[15:52] Maya Patel: we have a standard pilot agreement, i'll send that and the security packet.
[15:53] Priya Singh: one more technical: rerank uses cross-encoder style scoring or is it re-ranking using pairwise?
[15:53] Liam Chen: it's a cross-encoder style where the model scores query+candidate pairs; we offer single-pass cross-encoders and distilled bi-encoder hybrids for speed. the rerank endpoint abstracts that away but you can pick model families.
[15:54] Carlos Ruiz: do you have any customers with multi-lingual corpora?
[15:54] Liam Chen: yes we have several; we recommend multi-lingual embedding variants and verify with your eval set.
[15:55] Maya Patel: recap — we'll send pricing + pilot contract, Liam will share benchmark spreadsheet and optimal embedding dims, and Omnify will provide sample dataset and queries.
[15:56] Tom Keller: next meeting to kick off pilot 2026-12-07, we'll confirm time by email.
[15:56] Maya Patel: perfect thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts.
[15:57] End of recording.
